title: Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graces 22nd Convocation of SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Chennai
subtitle:
Strategic technologies like Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Technologies will shape the future: Vice President
Research achieves its highest purpose when it serves society : Vice President
Youth have a defining role in the journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047 : Vice President
Higher education has expanded significantly since 2014 : Vice President
“Do not merely prepare yourself for the future; prepare yourself to shape the future”: Vice President
“Nation First – Rashtra Pratham” should remain the guiding principle : Vice President
Vice President Expresses Deep Pain Over Student’s Murder Linked to Drug-Related Whistleblowing in Tamil Nadu; Urges All to Say No to Drugs
body_text:
The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the 22nd Convocation of S.R.M. Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) at Kattankulathur, Chengalpattu near Chennai and called upon graduating students to use their knowledge, skills and innovation for nation-building, guided by the principle of ‘Nation First – Rashtra Pratham’.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the 22nd Convocation of S.R.M. Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) at Kattankulathur, Chengalpattu near Chennai today. The Vice President said the greatest strength of Bharat is its people, particularly its youth. Sharing… pic.twitter.com/8yi607z7he — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 16, 2026
Addressing the graduating students, the Vice President said a convocation is much more than the award of degrees. It celebrates years of perseverance, discipline and learning while marking the beginning of a lifelong journey of responsibility and service.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated SRMIST for creating an academic ecosystem that promotes interdisciplinary learning, creativity, entrepreneurship and critical thinking. He noted the institution’s growing focus on Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Technologies, semiconductor research, robotics, biotechnology and sustainable development, saying these fields would shape future economies and societies.
The Vice President appreciated SRMIST’s emphasis on translating research into practical solutions that improve lives, strengthen industry and contribute to sustainable development. He said that research achieves its highest purpose when it serves society.
The Vice President said research becomes truly appreciable when it produces the right results, creates a meaningful impact on society and translates into practical benefits for people.
Recalling India’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Vice President said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India provided COVID-19 vaccines to more than 100 countries. He said India did not seek to commercialise the humanitarian assistance. Recalling a conversation with the Speaker of Kenya recently, who had expressed gratitude for India’s vaccine assistance, he said many Western countries had not provided similar support to poorer nations. He added that India’s efforts helped safeguard humanity and reiterated that India stands for peace, development and the welfare of humanity.
The Vice President said the Prime Minister had told him that AIIMS should be available across the country, so that medical facilities and medical education could reach people across India.
The Vice President highlighted the expansion of higher education in the country since 2014. He said that 16 IIITs, 8 Central Universities, 8 IIMs, 7 IITs, 2 IISERs, 1 NIT and 12 AIIMS have been established during this period. Bharat today has more than 1,425 universities, 54,000 colleges and 16,850 standalone institutions, he said.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighted the substantial increase in women’s enrolment in higher education, from 1.57 crore in 2014-15 to 2.24 crore in 2023-24, an increase of 42.2 per cent. He said the increasing number of women receiving degrees and medals at convocation ceremonies was a welcome development.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the graduates were entering a defining phase in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047. He said the vision of a developed, innovative, inclusive and self-reliant Bharat calls upon every young Indian to contribute to nation-building.
The Vice President said the greatest strength of Bharat is its people, particularly its youth. Sharing his message with the graduating students, he said: “Do not merely prepare yourself for the future; prepare yourself to shape the future.”
He also urged students to stay away from drugs and all forms of substance abuse, and called upon them to choose “discipline over distraction, purpose over temptation, and excellence over easy shortcuts.”
The Vice President said the recent incident in Tamil Nadu in which a student was murdered for sharing information about the drug trade was deeply painful. He said he felt as though he had lost a member of his own family.
Calling upon graduates to make ‘Nation First – Rashtra Pratham’ their guiding principle, the Vice President said their knowledge, innovation and hard work should contribute to the progress, security and prosperity of Bharat. He urged them to uphold constitutional values, respect diversity, strengthen national unity and place the larger national interest above narrow self-interest.
In his concluding remarks, the Vice President urged graduates to carry with them the timeless Indian values of Gyaan (Knowledge), Kartavya (Duty), Karuna (Compassion) and Seva (Service).
On the occasion, the Vice President presented an Honorary Degree Certificate to Shri R. Velusamy, President, Automotive Business, Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd., and conferred medals, ranks and degrees upon the graduates. He also administered the ‘Say No to Drugs’ pledge to the graduates and students.
Governor of Tamil Nadu and Keralam, Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar; Chancellor, SRMIST, Dr. T. R. Paarivendhar; Pro-Chancellor (Administration), Dr. Ravi Pachamuthu; Pro-Chancellor (Academics), Dr. P. Sathyanarayanan; Vice-Chancellor, Dr. C. Muthamizhchelvan; and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

enrichment.summary: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the 22nd Convocation of SRM Institute of Science and Technology near Chennai, urging graduates to embrace 'Nation First' as their guiding principle and highlighting the role of AI, quantum technologies and research in nation-building. He cited data on the expansion of higher education institutions and women's enrolment since 2014, and expressed grief over a student's murder in Tamil Nadu linked to drug-related whistleblowing, administering a 'Say No to Drugs' pledge.
enrichment.context:
This is a routine convocation address by the Vice President, a ceremonial function he performs periodically at various universities. Such speeches typically combine generic exhortations to youth, references to government achievements in education and health infrastructure, and topical remarks on current events—in this case a tragic drug-related murder case in Tamil Nadu. The cited figures on higher education expansion (new IITs, IIMs, AIIMS, universities) and rising women's enrolment reflect government messaging on education sector growth since 2014, which aspirants may encounter in other contexts, but this speech itself introduces no new policy or data beyond reiterating known figures.

The reference to India's COVID-19 vaccine diplomacy (Vaccine Maitri) and the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision are recurring themes in official addresses, useful as context but not new developments. The mention of the Tamil Nadu student's murder over drug trade whistleblowing reflects ongoing concerns about narcotics-related crime and vigilante justice against informants, an internal security and social issue, though the speech itself does not announce any policy response.
